stack: Go 1.x (parent ultron-ap monolith) + html/template + HTMX + SQLite (modernc.org/sqlite). No new runtime dependencies introduced by this feature.

technical_debt.substitution: TC-IE-006h/006f/006e DOM rendering tests substituted with HTTP-level fragment assertions on the rendered HTML (string searches for severity ordering, .verdict-card count, 'All operational indicators clear' copy). The project has no headless-browser stack — adding Playwright/chromedp for a single set of TCs would impose a heavy dev-dependency.
technical_debt.reason: The Go test suite renders the same html/template the browser would receive; assertions check document order, escaping, and empty state without booting a browser. Equivalent to the lan-devices precedent.

technical_debt.substitution: axe-core / Lighthouse contrast scan deferred. Severity badges reuse parent FR-009 design tokens (bg-danger, text-yellow-400, text-blue-400) which the parent UI's contrast tests already cover.
technical_debt.reason: axe-core requires a headless browser; same dependency-cost reasoning as the lan-devices manifest. The fragment test asserts an explicit severity text label is present (NFR-020 AC-003), so colour is never the sole communicator.

technical_debt.substitution: 24-hour Pi soak / pprof allocation profile not executed in this Phase 4 session. TC-IE-011e covers the zero-alloc invariant via testing.AllocsPerRun against the compiled rule closure; TC-IE-001e covers the 100-tick wall-clock budget.
technical_debt.reason: Long-running validation belongs to deployment verification on hardware, not unit/integration tests. The synthetic 1-hour idle run (TC-IE-009e, 720 ticks) is the equivalent CI-deterministic substitution.

technical_debt.substitution: Bundled severity distribution differs from the spec example (FR-047 AC-006 example: 5 critical / 4 warn / 1 info). Implemented as 3 critical / 5 warn / 2 info — closer to the actual operational expectations: container_failed and temp_warning are info because container restarts and a 70 °C temperature are not action-now events; service_failed and disk_critical remain critical.
technical_debt.reason: The AC explicitly says 'each rule has a severity assigned' — the count is informational. Operational behaviour matches the AC: thermal/disk-critical/service-failed are critical; warnings are recoverable; info is observational.

technical_debt.substitution: Engine evaluation is driven inline by the existing SSE broadcast loop (server/sse.go::buildSSEPayloadWithOptions calls evalInsightsTick), not by a dedicated subscription channel from metrics.Collector. Service.Start(ctx, tickC, snapFn) is exposed for future use but unused in v1 wiring.
technical_debt.reason: metrics.Collector does not currently expose a tick channel or callback. Adding one would touch a parent contract for one downstream consumer; reusing the SSE broker tick (which already runs at sseInterval, defaulting to the same 5 s cadence) satisfies FR-039 AC-001 ('verdict-set published within 5 s') without changing the collector API.

technical_debt.substitution: swap_pct, lan_device_offline_count, and loss_pct telemetry variables are not yet projected from any existing collector — the SSE adapter (server/sse.go::evalInsightsTick) only populates cpu_pct, ram_pct, temp_c, disk_root_pct, services_failed, containers_failed, wan_gateway_ok, wan_cloudflare_ok. The memory_pressure / sustained_packet_loss / lan_offline_burst rules therefore stay quiet in production until those variables are wired. FR-041 AC-002 — 'missing var resolves to false, never error' — is preserved by the lang package; the rules degrade gracefully.
technical_debt.reason: Bringing in the WAN packet-loss and LAN-devices feeds is a separate integration step. The rule definitions ship now; the dashboard surface ships now; the data-source wiring is incremental and does not require a v2 binary.
